1.What is Exception? Write a program for exception handling

An exception is an event that occurs during the execution of a program and disrupts the normal flow of instructions. 
Exceptions are handled using try, catch, finally, throw, and throws keywords to prevent the program from terminating abruptly.

Example:

package assignment;

public class ExceptionConcept {

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		// TODO Auto-generated method stub
		try {
			int a = 5/0;
			System.out.println(a);
		}catch(Exception e) {
			System.out.println("Cannot Divided By Zero");
		}finally {
			System.out.println("Finally block executed");
		}
	}

}

Output:

Cannot Divided By Zero
Finally block executed

2.What is Collections? Write a program to remove duplicate names using Collections

Collections in Java is a framework that provides classes and interfaces to store, manage, and manipulate groups of objects efficiently. 

It includes useful data structures such as List, Set, Queue, and Map.

List – Stores ordered elements and allows duplicates. 

Set – Stores unique elements (no duplicates). 

Map – Stores key-value pairs.

Example:

package assignment;
import java.util.*;
public class Collections {

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		// TODO Auto-generated method stub
		HashSet<String> name = new HashSet<>();
		name.add("Sudharsan");
		name.add("Vishal");
		name.add("Sandeep");
		name.add("Vishal"); // duplicate
		name.add("Kishore");
		name.add("Sandeep"); // duplicate
		name.add("Subiksha");
		System.out.println(name);
	}

}

Output:

[Sudharsan, Sandeep, Subiksha, Kishore, Vishal]
